newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hoiu, Tallinna lead active Estonian market.
newsitem.headline: Hoiu, Tallinna lead active Estonian market.

text.p: Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank led Estonia's bourse on Friday as an active market responded to reports that the two were holding unofficial merger talks.
Total volume was 54.2 million kroons and the Talse gained 0.28 percent to close at 278.71.

A local business paper reported on Friday morning that Hoiu and Tallinna were in unofficial merger talks. Hoiu donwplayed the rumours in the morning and Tallinna denied them in the afternoon, but the market had already moved.
"The newspaper article saying that unofficial talks had been held between Tallinna Pank and Hoiupank had the biggest impact today," one dealer said.
Hoiupank closed one kroon higher at 152.00 kroons in trade of 12.2 million kroons.

Over the short three-day week, Hoiupank's share price rose by almost to eight percent on news that Sweden's Swedbank will increase its holding in the bank by seven percent to hold 19.9 percent of its stock.
Tallinna Pank's share price peaked at 70 kroons during trade to fall back to 64.75 kroons, 1.25 kroons higher than Thursday's close.
Hansapank saw trade of 9.6 million kroons to close at 148.50 kroons or 0.75 kroons higher.
Brokers see further gains ahead of the release of six-month results from the banking sector.
